reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes hot-corrosion behaviour of Al2O3/Cr2O3-forming high-entropy alloy coatings, not Q235 steel or Fe-oxide/spinel scales. No evidence is provided to support the formation, adherence, or barrier performance of an Fe-oxide layer on Q235 under the proposed conditions, nor the differential temperature effect. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Annealing Q235 steel in air at 700 °C forms a uniform, adherent Fe-oxide/spinel passive layer.
A uniform, adherent oxide scale acts as a barrier against salt infiltration and reduces corrosion mass loss.
Pre-oxidized Q235 will show reduced mass change vs. untreated Q235 in 75% Na2SO4 + 25% NaCl at 700–900 °C.
The protective effect is specific to high-temperature salt exposure and less critical at room temperature.
